# VM instruction reference

*Generated by `perl instref.pl` from `instset.h` (the specification: change that, then run `make vmref`; `make vmref-check` fails when this file is out of date). Do not edit this file.*

The VM (`vm.[ch]`) is a stack machine that runs the code the code generator (`codegen.c`, `cgen*.c`) makes from the syntax tree (`docs/compiler-and-vm.md`). This page lists every instruction: its code, the stack effect, how its parameter is used, and the details of the specification. The machine monitor (`MONITOR`) and `vmasm.[ch]` (the VM assembler / decoder) use the same mnemonics.

## The machine

- **Data stack:** items of 64 bit: a floating-point number (`n`) or a pointer to a string on the heap (`s`). An instruction removes its operands; an instruction with a string operand frees it. Strings are binary safe (a length, no terminator), at most 65535 bytes.
- **Return stack:** 32 bit code addresses (`a`) and, for a call of a `PROC` / `FUNC`, the context that restores the parameter variables. `GOSUB` pushes on it too (`RTRP` tells the two apart).
- **Code and data segments:** 32 bit offsets that grow on demand. Variables live in `vars.[ch]` and are addressed by a variable number (`varoffs`). All multi-byte values in code are **big endian**.
- **Notation** (as in FORTH): `( n1 n2 -- n )` is "takes n1, then n2; leaves n"; `R( a -- )` is the return stack; `n` number, `s` string, `a` address, `inx ... ndim` array subscripts followed by their count.
- **Resumable:** the VM stops cleanly between instructions (single step, breakpoints, `WAIT`, timers, requests to the host such as `LOAD` / `RUN` / `NEW` / `EDIT` / `MONITOR`), so a host loop can run it again with `vm_resume()`. Run-time errors go to `ON ERROR` handlers or stop the program with the message and line number.

## Encoding

```
<ins> [ <ext> ] [ <hi> <lo> ]          or, with the W flag:   <ins> [ <ext> ] [ <b3> <b2> <b1> <b0> ]

instruction byte:   P C E W | I I I I
```

| Flag | Bit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| P | 0x80 | a parameter field follows |
| C | 0x40 | the parameter or stack is of the *code* (return stack, code address), not the data kind |
| E | 0x20 | extended instruction: one more byte follows; the 4 bits of the instruction byte become the high bits of a 12 bit code, the extension byte the low 8 |
| W | 0x10 | wide: the parameter has 32 bits instead of 16 (only with P) |
| I | 0x0F | the instruction field (the 16 basic instructions, or the high 4 bits of an extended one) |

The code generator uses the short form where a value fits (variable numbers, small data offsets, small immediates) and the wide form for everything that can exceed 65535: code addresses (always, they are patched after the instruction was generated), data offsets, line numbers and large immediates. In an extended instruction the C and P bits belong to the instruction as listed below.

## Basic instructions (code in the instruction byte, bits 0..3)

| Code | Mnemonic | Stack | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x0 | `BRK` |  | a breakpoint (reports "Breakpoint"; C and P ignored) |
| 0x1 | `NOP` |  | no operation (C and P ignored) |
| 0x2 | `PHPA` | `( -- n ) or R( -- a )` | push the parameter as an address: C=0 onto the data stack (as a number), C=1 onto the return stack (as an integer); P must be set |
| 0x3 | `PHIM` | `( -- n )` | push an immediate: 17 bits (C is the 17th bit, sign-extended) or, with W, a signed 32 bit value (C ignored); converted to a number |
| 0x4 | `BRIA` |  | branch to an immediate code address (17 bits with C, or 32 bits with W; the generator always uses the wide form); out of range is a run-time error |
| 0x5 | `BRIR` |  | branch relative to the following instruction (signed 17 / 32 bit offset) |
| 0x6 | `JPCC` | `( n -- ) R( a -- )` | quick conditional jump: continue at the code address from the return stack if the number is nonzero (C=1, P=0) |
| 0x7 | `JUMP` | `R( a -- )` | quick jump: pull a code address from the return stack and go there (C=1, P=0); `GOSUB` / `RETURN` use it |
| 0x8 | `DROP` | `( n -- ) or R( a -- )` | drop items (parameter = how many, default 1) from the data stack (C=0, 8 bytes each) or the return stack (C=1) |
| 0x9 | `LINE` |  | set the current line number (the first instruction of every program line; P set, C=0); errors, `TRACE`, `ERL` and the monitor use it |
| 0xA | `LAN` | `( n -- n )` | load a number from a code or data address on the stack (C selects the segment; the address is a floating-point number) |
| 0xB | `LIAN` | `( n -- n )` | load a signed integer from an address and convert it to a number |
| 0xC | `LUAN` | `( n -- n )` | load an unsigned integer from an address and convert it to a number |
| 0xD | `LAS` | `( n -- s )` | load a string constant from an address (a new heap string) |
| 0xE | `FRES` | `( s -- )` | free a string pointer from the data stack (C=0) |
| 0xF | | | reserved |

`PHPA` has two named forms in the code generator: `PHPA.C` (C=1, the return stack) and `PHPA.D` (C=0, the data stack).

## Extended instructions (12 bit code)

The first group (0x01x, 0x02x) is arithmetic, logic and comparison; 0x1xx are the variable, call, I/O, string, system and host instructions. "C P" is the flag pair the instruction is generated with (`P=0/1`: both forms exist). The stack effect is in the notation above.

| Code | Mnemonic | Stack | C P | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x010 | `NEG` | `( n -- n )` | C=0 P=0 | numerical negation |
| 0x011 | `NOT` | `( n -- n )` | C=0 P=0 | bitwise NOT |
| 0x012 | `LSH` | `( n1 n2 -- n )` | C=0 P=0 | left shift |
| 0x013 | `RSH` | `( n1 n2 -- n )` | C=0 P=0 | right shift |
| 0x014 | `ADD` | `( n1 n2 -- n )` | C=0 P=0 | numerical addition |

## Details of the extended instructions

The text of the specification, instruction by instruction (only those that have more to say than the table).

### `CALF` (0x112)

```
Operation:
  - the return address is put on the return stack
  - the arguments are pulled from the stack and written into a temporary space
  - the context for the call is created and pushed onto the return stack (pointer):
  - contains the varoffs and content of each regular parameter variable before the call
  (saving array state isn't necessary)
  - each regular parameter variable is set to one of the values from the temporary space
  - code execution continues with the code of the function
```

### `RETF` (0x113)

```
  - the context is pulled from the return stack, and variable contents are restored
  - execution resumes with the instruction after the CALF instruction.
  - the data stack is not affected (a result placed there will still exist afterwards)
```

### `ERAS` (0x116)

```
  resets all elements of the array to their initial state (0 or the empty string)
```

### `RSTR` (0x11F)

```
  P=0: the pointer goes back to the first item; P=1: to the item at the given data
  offset (0xFFFFFFFF = behind the last item). With a parameter the instruction is wide
  (the offset is patched in when all DATA items are known).
  DATA items are records in the data segment, chained in program order:
  <type.8> <next.32> <payload>, type 0 = number (8 bytes, big endian IEEE double),
  type 1 = string (NUL-terminated text); <next> is the data offset of the next item or
  0xFFFFFFFF. The first item is found through codegen_t.datafirst (0xFFFFFFFF = no DATA).
  Reading behind the last item, or an item of the wrong type, is a run time error.
```

### `CHRS` (0x126)

```
  n must be 0..255, else a run time error (strings are binary-safe: they have a length)
```

### `SMID` (0x12E)

```
The variable is a string variable (ndim = 0) or an element of a string array (the
subscripts, as for WSAE). The string s replaces characters of the variable's value:
  SLFT: the first  min( n, LEN(s), LEN(var) ) characters
  SRGT: the last   min( n, LEN(s), LEN(var) ) characters
  SMID: min( len, LEN(s), LEN(var) - start + 1 ) characters beginning at <start> (counts
  from 1); a negative <len> stands for the rest of the string
The characters come from the beginning of s, the length of the variable doesn't change.
n < 0, start < 1 or start > LEN(var) are errors.
```

### `INPL` (0x134)

```
  Prints the prompt (NUL-terminated text in the data segment, to the current channel, see
  PCHN) and reads a line from the current channel into the VM's input buffer. The
  instruction is the restart point of the INPUT statement (see INPN).
```

### `INPS` (0x136)

```
  Fields of the input line are separated by commas; a field starting with a double quote
  extends to the closing quote (the quotes are removed). A numeric field is a decimal
  number with optional sign, fraction and exponent, surrounded by blanks; an empty field
  is 0. A string field that isn't quoted is trimmed of blanks at both ends.
  If the field is missing, or isn't a number for INPN, the VM prints "?Redo from start"
  and execution continues at the INPL instruction of the statement (fields already
  stored stay stored).
```

### `INPE` (0x137)

```
  If the line has more fields than the statement has variables, prints "?Extra ignored".
  Releases the input buffer.
```

### `GETK` (0x138)

```
  (GET stores it directly in a string variable, or converts it with ASC for a numeric one)
```

### `LOAD` (0x139)

```
  Asks the host to replace the program by the one in file <s> and to run it from the
  beginning (all variables cleared). The VM stores the request (vm_t.request) and stops;
  the host that called vm_run() carries it out. An empty name is an error.
```

### `RUNP` (0x13A)

```
  Asks the host to run the stored program from a line number (n >= 0) or a label (name s,
  if not empty) after clearing all variables; ( "" -1 ) = from the beginning. Same
  mechanism as LOAD.
```

### `LIST` (0x13B)

```
  Lists the stored program through the host (list callback) to the current output channel.
  (s1,n1) is the first line, (s2,n2) the last one: a label name (empty = none) or a line
  number (-1 = none). A side that is not given is unbounded; a label stands for the line it
  is defined in. Both sides given = an inclusive range.
```

### `NEW` (0x13C)

```
  Asks the host to delete the program and the variables; the VM stores the request and
  stops (like LOAD), the program is not continued.
```

### `CLR` (0x13D)

```
  Numeric variables become 0, strings "", arrays are emptied (they keep their dimensions);
  labels, functions and the compiler's hidden variables are kept.
```

### `DELE` (0x13E)

```
  Deletes the lines in the range (same operands as LIST) through the host (delete callback),
  then ends the run: the stored program no longer matches the code that is running.
```

### `RENM` (0x13F)

```
  Renumbers the lines of the range (operands as for LIST) with the new numbers starting at the
  first line of the range (10 if the start is not given), through the host (renumber
  callback); then ends the run like DELE. step is a number >= 1.
```

### `EDIT` (0x140)

```
  Asks the host to let the user edit the line given by a line number (n >= 0) or a label
  (name s, if not empty); ( "" -1 ) = no target. Stores a request like RUNP and ends the run.
```

### `MON` (0x141)

```
  Stores a request for the host (like NEW) and ends the run.
```

### `SND` (0x142)

```
  1 SOUND ( ch freq beats vol endfreq -- )   a tone: channel 1..8, 20..20000 Hz (0 = a rest),
  beats >= 0 (the channel's next event follows after that; -1 = held until the next event), volume 0..1; endfreq != 0 (20..20000,
  needs beats > 0): the pitch glides to it during the tone
  2 PLAY ( s1 .. sn n -- )           n music strings (1..8): string i plays on channel i, all
  voices start together (the strings are parsed first: a wrong one queues nothing, see mml.h)
  3 WAVE ( ch wave -- )              wave type 0..3 (sine, square, triangle, noise) or the instrument 4..63
  4 TEMPO ( bpm -- )                 beats per minute 1..1000 (the unit of the beats of SOUND)
  5 OFF ( ch -- )                    silence the channel now and forget what is queued; 0 = all
  6 SYNC ( ch1 .. chn n -- )         line up the channels' time (so that they start together)
  7 PITCH ( ch freq -- )             at once: the pitch of the channel, 20..20000 Hz
  8 VOLUME ( ch vol -- )             at once: the volume of the note, 0..1
  9 ENVELOPE ( ch a d s r -- )       attack, decay (s), sustain level 0..1, release (s), each time
  0..60; a < 0 = back to the default
  10 VIBRATO ( ch rate depth -- )    rate 0..100 Hz, depth 0..24 semitones (0 = off)
  11 TREMOLO ( ch rate depth -- )    rate 0..100 Hz, depth 0..1 (0 = off)
  12 SFXDEF ( n s -- )               store the music string s as effect n (1..64)
  13 SFXPLAY ( n ch -- )             play effect n on channel ch (0 = a free one)
  14 INSTDEF ( n s -- )              define instrument n (4..63) from the definition string s (mml_parse_inst(), see mml.h);
  the VM keeps it; the channels that use n get a snapshot queued at their own time (vm_sound_t.setinst)
  15 INSTRESET ( n -- )              the factory instrument n (4..63) again
  16 CUTOFF ( ch mult seconds -- )   the filter cutoff of an instrument channel glides to mult * note frequency (0.01..64; -1 =
  back to the instrument's own) within seconds (0..60; 0 = at once); vm_sound_t.setcut
  17 PAN ( ch pos -- )               the stereo position of the channel, -1 (left) .. 1 (right), 0 = centre; vm_sound_t.setpan
  Everything but 7 and 8 is queued at the channel's time line; all return at once. Without sound
  callbacks the arguments are only checked. A bad argument is "Illegal argument".
```

### `PLNG` (0x143)

```
  -1 while channel 1..8 sounds or has events queued or a sequence still running, else 0 (also
  without sound callbacks). Other channels are "Illegal argument".
```

### `WAIT` (0x144)

```
  Sleeps for n/60 seconds (n >= 0, at most 216000 = one hour; the unit of TI) without using the
  processor. The interrupt callback is asked every 10 ms, so Break ends the wait ("Break").
```

### `MRG` (0x145)

```
  Merges the program file <s> into the stored program through the host (merge callback); the
  parameter is 1 for APPEND (the file's lines are numbered behind the last stored line). Then ends the
  run: the stored program no longer matches the code that is running. An empty name is an error.
```

### `CHN` (0x146)

```
  Asks the host to load the file <s1> (parameter 1: merge it into the stored program) and to run the
  result from the label s2 ("" = none) or the line n (-1 = none), or from the beginning; the values of
  the variables that both programs have are kept. Request VMREQ_CHAIN, like LOAD.
```

### `FILS` (0x147)

```
  Lists the files named by <s> ("" = the current directory) through the host (files callback) to
  the current output channel: size, time and name, oldest first. The run goes on.
```

### `TMR` (0x148)

```
  AFTER / EVERY: arms timer 0..3 to run the handler at the code address on the return stack after
  delay ticks (1/60 s; delay > 0). Parameter bit 0 = EVERY (repeats), bit 1 = GOTO (the handler is
  jumped to; else it is called like GOSUB with the interrupted address as return address and
  only timers with a higher number can interrupt it). A timer that is set again is replaced.
```

### `TMRO` (0x149)

```
  AFTER OFF / EVERY OFF: clears timer 0..3 if it is of the kind in parameter bit 0 (1 = EVERY), or
  all timers of that kind if the operand is -1.
```

### `RMN` (0x14A)

```
  REMAIN(): the ticks (1/60 s, rounded up) until timer 0..3 is due, 0 if it is not active. The
  timer is cleared (AFTER and EVERY alike). Other numbers are "Illegal argument".
```

### `HLT` (0x14B)

```
  Ends the run (pc = end of the code). The compiler puts one at the end of a program: END and the
  end of the last line branch to it, so the code of a direct mode line, which is placed behind the
  program, is not entered by running off the end of the program.
```

### `OPEN` (0x14C)

```
  Opens file <name$> (with an optional "driver:" prefix, else the ADDRESS driver) as channel n
  (1..255): mode "I" = input, "O" = output (truncates), "A" = append, "U" = update (read and write, no truncation), "R" = random
  file with records of reclen bytes (0 = 128; reclen must be 0 for the other modes); case does not matter.
  Errors: "File already open", "Bad file number", "Bad file mode", "Device not found", "File not
  found", "Permission denied", ... (docs/io-subsystem.md).
```

### `CLOS` (0x14D)

```
  Closes channel n (1..255; closing one that is not open is not an error), or all channels (not
  channel 0) for n = -1.
```

### `INPW` (0x14E)

```
  LINE INPUT: after INPL, pushes the rest of the line that was read (commas are not separators).
```

### `EOFN` (0x14F)

```
  EOF(n): -1 at the end of the data of input channel n, else 0.
```

### `LOFN` (0x150)

```
  LOF(n): the length in bytes.
```

### `LOCN` (0x151)

```
  LOC(n): the number of bytes read or written so far.
```

### `INPD` (0x152)

```
  INPUT$(count, #n): count characters from channel n (channel 0 = the keyboard, waits for keys);
  fewer than count at the end of a file is "Input past end".
```

### `ADDR` (0x153)

```
  ADDRESS name: the default driver for names without a prefix. Parameter 1 = no operand: swap the
  current and the previous default (ADDRESS alone).
```

### `ADRS` (0x154)

```
  ADDRESS$.
```

### `FOP` (0x155)

```
  Parameter = kind: 1 KILL ( name$ -- ), 2 RENAME ( from$ to$ -- ), 3 MKDIR ( name$ -- ),
  4 CHDIR ( name$ -- ), 5 SEEK ( n pos -- ): bytes from the start of channel n. Names may have a
  "driver:" prefix. Errors: "File not found", "Permission denied", "File already exists",
  "Not the same device", "Not supported by device", "Bad position", ...
```

### `FLD` (0x156)

```
  FIELD: the parameter is the variable number of a plain string variable. Channel n must be a
  random file. first = 1 starts a new FIELD statement: the old bindings of the channel are dropped and
  the offset is 0; every binding takes the next len bytes ("Field overflow" behind the record).
```

### `LRS` (0x157)

```
  The parameter is the variable number. Puts s into the variable's slice of the record buffer, padded
  with spaces (right = 0: left justified, 1: right justified), cut to the width, and into the variable.
  A variable that is not bound keeps its length: s is justified within it.
```

### `REC` (0x158)

```
  Parameter 0 = GETREC, 1 = PUTREC. rec = 0: the record behind the last one. GETREC then assigns the
  slices to the bound variables (their whole width). Errors: "Input past end", "Bad record
  number", "Bad file mode" (not a random file).
```

### `ERRT` (0x159)

```
  ON ERROR. Parameter 0 = OFF; 1 = GOSUB, 2 = GOTO: the handler's code address is on the return stack
  (like TMR). A run time error then does not end the run: the data stack and open function calls are
  dropped, ERR$ / ERL are set and the handler runs. GOTO: the handler is entered and the trap is off
  until ON ERROR is executed again; GOSUB: the return address is the start of the next program line,
  the trap is off while the handler runs and on again after its RETURN. Not caught: Break.
```

### `ERRS` (0x15B)

```
  ERR$: e.g. "Division by zero" (without "?" and the line).
```

### `PACK` (0x15C)

```
  MKI$ / MKL$ / MKS$ / MKD$, parameter 1 / 2 / 3 / 4: 2, 4, 4 or 8 bytes, big endian (network byte
  order). 1 = 16 bit integer (n in -32768..65535, the low 16 bits), 2 = 32 bit integer (n in
  -2147483648..4294967295), 3 = IEEE 754 single, 4 = IEEE 754 double. Else "Illegal argument" (Overflow).
```

### `UNPK` (0x15D)

```
  CVI / CVL / CVS / CVD (parameter 1..4): reads the first 2, 4, 4 or 8 bytes of the string (more are
  ignored, fewer are "Illegal argument"). CVI and CVL are signed (use "AND 65535" for the unsigned value).
```

### `GFXC` (0x15E)

```
  Parameter = the GFXOP_* number of gfxops.h. The arguments are on the stack in source order (numbers and
  strings as the signature of the operation says; omitted optional ones are GFX_NONE = -1e9). The VM
  checks the types and calls the host (vm_t.gfx); an operation with a result string (GRAB, TILE GET,
  SPRITE GET, TXT SAVE) leaves it on the stack, the code that follows stores it in the variable.
```

### `GFXQ` (0x15F)

```
  Parameter = the GFXQ_* number: RGB (computed by the VM), POINT, TILE(x,y) and the selector functions of
  GFX(), TXT(), SPRITE() (docs/graphics-subsystem.md). The host answers all but RGB.
```

### `DSGN` (0x160)

```
  DESIGN SPRITE (1) / TILE (2) / CHAR (3): pops the number and, for the parameter 1 + 4, the color base;
  the following DROW rows are collected until the picture is complete (24 rows of 16, or 12 of 8).
```

### `DROW` (0x161)

```
  @ "row": 16 (8 for CHAR) characters of . 1-9 A-F o; when the last row has arrived the image is defined.
```

### `COLT` (0x162)

```
  ON COLLISION: parameter 0 = OFF; 1 = GOSUB, 2 = GOTO with the handler's address on the return stack.
  ON MOUSE: the same with the parameter bit 2 added (4 = OFF, 5 = GOSUB, 6 = GOTO). ON JOY 8, ON KEY 16, ON UI 32, ON SPRITE 64 (65 GOSUB, 66 GOTO).
```

### `IDIV` (0x163)

```
  a \ b: both operands are truncated toward zero, the quotient too; b = 0 (after truncating) is "Division by zero".
```

### `MOD` (0x164)

```
  a MOD b: both truncated toward zero, the result has the sign of a; b = 0 is "Division by zero".
```

### `MATH` (0x165)

```
  Parameter: 1 INT (floor), 2 FIX (toward zero), 3 ABS, 4 SGN, 5 SQR, 6 SIN, 7 COS, 8 TAN, 9 ATN (arc tangent),
  10 EXP, 11 LOG (natural), 12 RND, 13 PI ( -- pi ). Angles in radians. SQR of a negative number, LOG of a number
  <= 0 are "Illegal argument", a result that is not finite is "Overflow". RND(x): x > 0 the next random
  number 0 <= r < 1; x = 0 the last one again; x < 0 starts the sequence over from the seed x.
```

### `RAND` (0x166)

```
  Parameter 1: seed popped, the sequence is the same for the same seed; 0: seeded from the clock.
```

### `ANGM` (0x167)

```
  DEG (1), RAD (2), GRAD (3): the unit of the angles of SIN, COS, TAN and ATN (a property of the runtime: RUN
  and NEW return to RAD). In degrees and gradians the multiples of a quarter turn are exact (SIN(90) = 1,
  COS(90) = 0); TAN of an odd multiple of a quarter turn is "Overflow".
```

### `AFLT` (0x169)

```
  FOR EACH uses the two. An index outside 0 .. n-1 is "Subscript out of range".
```

### `DTIM` (0x16D)

```
  Parameter 1: "HH:MM:SS", 2: "YYYY-MM-DD", 3: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS".
```

### `LOCL` (0x16E)

```
  The value of the (numeric, integer or string) variable is saved in the context of the call and given back when
  the call ends (RETF, or an error that unwinds the call); the variable starts as 0 or "". Outside a call it is
  the error "LOCAL outside a procedure".
```

### `RSM` (0x16F)

```
  Only in an error handler (ON ERROR) and only if the error happened outside a function call. 0 goes to the start
  of the statement that failed (the innermost one: the code generator keeps a table of the statements), 1 to the
  first instruction behind it, 2 to the code address on the return stack. Then the handler is over: a GOSUB handler
  drops its return address, a GOTO handler is armed again. "RESUME without error" otherwise.
```

### `STOP` (0x170)

```
  Like the Break key: the run ends with "Break in line n", but the state of the VM (data stack, return stack, calls in
  progress, the next instruction) is kept for CONT. STOP inside the code of a direct mode line is a plain Break.
```

### `CONT` (0x171)

```
  Takes the state STOP (or the Break key) kept and goes on there; "Can't continue" if there is none. The state is lost when the
  stored program changes and when a program starts (RUN, NEW, LOAD, CHAIN). Timers and the ON ERROR handler end with the run
  and are not restored.
```

### `TRON` (0x172)

```
  While on, every LINE instruction prints "[n]".
```

### `AUTO` (0x173)

```
  Leaves a request for the host (VMREQ_AUTO) and ends the run; -1 = default (10).
```

### `POKE` (0x176)

```
  The RAM is a block of VM_RAMSIZE bytes (1 MiB, zero, allocated at the first POKE, kept over direct mode lines, cleared by
  RUN/NEW/LOAD), addressed from 0; multi-byte values are big endian. size 1, 2: unsigned byte / word, 4: signed
  long, -4: single, -8: double precision float (an other size is "Illegal argument", a block that is not inside the RAM
  "Illegal address"). POKE of a string value writes its bytes (size is ignored); POKE of a number accepts the range of
  its size (signed or unsigned: the low bits are stored).
```

### `BLD` (0x177)

```
  BUILD: asks the host (build callback) to create the executable file <name> from the stored program (the run goes
  on). "Illegal argument" for an empty name, "BUILD is not available" without the callback; the host reports why a build
  failed ("Build failed"). The parameter is the kind of runtime: 0 = the host's own (default), 1 = WINDOW (SDL2), 2 = CONSOLE
  (no SDL: the executable runs without a window).
```

### `BYE` (0x178)

```
  BYE [code] / QUIT [code]: leaves a request for the host (VMREQ_QUIT, the exit code in reqline) and ends the run. The host ends the
  Engine (or the built program) with the code. "Illegal argument" unless the code is an integer 0..255.
```

### `ARGC` (0x179)

```
  The arguments the host gave the program (vm_t.argv without its first element, the program name); 0 if there are none.
```

### `ARGS` (0x17A)

```
  n = 0 is the program name, 1..ARGC the arguments; "" for a larger n; "Illegal argument" for a negative or fractional one.
```

### `ENVS` (0x17B)

```
  The value of the variable of the process (getenv), "" if it is not set. A name with a zero byte is "Illegal argument".
```

### `BRKM` (0x17C)

```
  Tells the VM and the host (vm_t.breakesc) whether ESC is the break key (1) or an ordinary key (0).
```

### `KEYD` (0x17D)

```
  KEY(name$): -1 if the key of that name (keystate.h: "A", "SPACE", "LEFT", "F1", "SHIFT", "ANY" ...) is down now, else 0; a name that
  is no key is "Illegal argument". The host answers (vm_t.keydown); without one it is the error "KEY is not available in this host" (the console host).
```

### `MTH2` (0x17E)

```
  Parameter 1 = MIN, 2 = MAX, 3 = ATAN2 (y = the first argument, x = the second; the angle is in the unit of DEG / RAD / GRAD), 4 = ROUND (x rounded to y decimals, halves away from zero; y < 0 rounds to tens, hundreds ...).
```

### `STRN` (0x17F)

```
  STRING$(n, c) and SPACE$(n). Parameter 0: c is a character code 0..255; 1: c is a string, its first byte is repeated
  (an empty string is "Illegal argument"); 2: SPACE$, the stack holds n only. n is 0..65535, else "Illegal argument".
```

### `ERRN` (0x180)

```
  ERR: 0 if there was none. The numbers are in the table errtab[] of vm.c (5 Illegal argument, 6 Overflow, 7 Out of memory, 9 Subscript out of range,
  11 Division by zero, 13 Type mismatch, ...); 255 for any other message; ERROR n gives n back.
```

### `ERRR` (0x181)

```
  ERROR n: an error with the text of number n (the table; "Error n" if the table has none), n = 1..255, else "Illegal argument". It is caught by ON ERROR like any other.
```

### `JOYQ` (0x182)

```
  JOY(name$, player): name is a button ("A" .. "RIGHT", "SHARE": -1 held / 0), an axis ("LX" "LY" "RX" "RY": -1 .. 1 with the dead zone, "LT" "RT": 0 .. 1) or one of
  CONNECTED (-1 / 0), BUTTONS / PRESSED / RELEASED (the buttons added up as bits; PRESSED and RELEASED are latched since the last call), COUNT (the pads
  plugged in) and EVENTS (a counter that ON JOY watches), DEADZONE (the setting). player is 1..4 ("Illegal argument" otherwise, except for COUNT and EVENTS);
  a player without a pad reads 0. An unknown name is "Illegal argument". The state is joy.h (no host callback).
```

### `JOYD` (0x183)

```
  JOY DEADZONE d: 0 .. 0.9 for all pads, else "Illegal argument".
```

### `FRAM` (0x184)

```
  FRAME n: waits until n more frames have begun (the host's frame counter, GFX("FRAME"); the console host counts 60 a second); n = 0 returns at once, 1 is the next refresh.
  Like WAIT it gives way to timer handlers and stops with Break; n is 0 .. 3600, else "Illegal argument".
```

### `JOYS` (0x185)

```
  JOY$(name$, player): "NAME" is the pad's name ("" for a player without a pad); other names are "Illegal argument"; player as for JOYQ.
```

### `KEYS` (0x186)

```
  KEY$("EVENT"): the oldest key event that has not been read: "+A" (the key went down) or "-A" (it was let go), the name as KEY("name") knows it ("A", "SPACE", "LEFT", "F5",
  "LSHIFT" ...); "" if there is none. The window queues the events (64 at most, a key repeat is none) while a program runs; other names are "Illegal argument";
  without a host that has key events (the console host) it is the error "KEY is not available in this host".
```

### `LIBS` (0x187)

```
  LIBRARIES [name$]: the empty string lists the libraries of the last compile (name, prefix, file); a name lists the PROCs, FUNCs and LABELs that library defines.
  The host does it through vm_t.libraries; without one it is the error "LIBRARIES is not available".
```

### `EXST` (0x188)

```
  EXISTS(name$): -1 if the name can be opened for reading through the I/O drivers (a "driver:" prefix works, ADDRESS names the default driver; no extension search: the name is taken as it is), else 0. An empty name is 0, not an error;
  it never raises a file error (that is what it is for: ON ERROR + RESUME does not work inside a PROC or FUNC).
```

### `PUSG` (0x189)

```
  Parameter 0: begins a formatted PRINT (the format string is taken from the stack; at most 255 bytes, else "Illegal argument");
  the PNUM / PSTR that follow with the parameter bit PRTARG_USING put each value into the next field of the format (the format
  starts again when it is used up) and the literal text around the fields; "Type mismatch" if a value does not fit the kind of
  field, "Illegal argument" if the format has no field. Parameter 1: ends it (prints the literal text behind the last field that was used).
```

### `FMTS` (0x18A)

```
  FORMAT$(value, format$): the value in the first field of a PRINT USING format, with the literal text around it (in front of the field and
  up to the next one behind it). Parameter 0: the value is a number, 1: a string. Same errors as PRINT USING.
```

### `CLPG` (0x18B)

```
  The text on the clipboard (the system's through the host's clipget callback, else the internal clipboard of clipboard.h; ISO-8859-15,
  LF line ends; empty if there is none; "String too long" over 65535 bytes).
```

### `CLPS` (0x18C)

```
  Puts the text on the clipboard (the host's clipset callback, else the internal clipboard).
```

### `TOOL` (0x18D)

```
  TOOL name$ [, arg$]: runs the tool (a BASIC program of the tools folder) in a fresh state and comes back when it ends: the stored program, its
  variables and the CONT state stay as they were. Parameter 0: the name only, 1: the argument is on the stack, too (the tool reads it as ARG$(1)).
  The host does it through vm_t.tool, which returns 0 or an error text; without such a callback (the console host) it is the error
  "TOOL is not available in the console host".
```

### `RTRP` (0x18E)

```
  A GOSUB made in the body of the procedure that has not returned yet (the return stack holds more than the call's own two entries: the return
  address and the context) is returned from like JUMP: the address is pulled and execution goes on there. Otherwise the instruction does nothing
  and the next instruction (a BRIA to the end of the procedure, as for EXIT PROC) leaves the procedure. The compiler emits RTRP + BRIA for every
  plain RETURN in a PROC / FUNC / multi-line DEF FN; in the main program a plain RETURN stays a JUMP.
```

### `INSR` (0x18F)

```
  INSTR([start,] hay$, needle$): the position (1 = first byte) of the first needle in hay at or after start, 0 if it is not there. Parameter 0: no start (it is 1);
  parameter 1: start is the first of the three values. start < 1 is "Illegal argument", start beyond the end of hay gives 0; an empty needle is found at start
  (if start is within hay). Binary safe (zero bytes are ordinary bytes), case sensitive.
```

### `INSS` (0x190)

```
  INSTRUMENT$(n): the definition string of instrument n (0..63) as it is now (the program's own or the factory one), in the form
  mml_inst_string() writes and INSTRUMENT n, a$ reads back; 0..3 give only "NAME SINE" etc. (the basic waves are not definable). Else "Illegal argument".
```

## Fused instructions

At run time `vm.c` maps the address of some instruction sequences (`RRNV;RRNV;ADD`, a counting loop test, one and two dimensional array element access, ...) to a **fused handler** through a lazily filled side table. The code does not change (the monitor, `LIST` and jumps into the middle of a sequence work), every handler checks its preconditions and falls back to the plain instruction, and fusing is off while single-stepping, with breakpoints, with a step limit and with `E1999_NOFUSE=1` in the environment. Details and the list of fused sequences: [compiler-and-vm.md](compiler-and-vm.md), "Fused instructions and array fast path"; `fusetest.sh` compares runs with and without fusing.
